clue.text: Series about Wood as a director of music?

indicators.note: the word series is put around the next pieces, so it surrounds them

parts.note: a chapter can mean a series, as in a chapter of accidents
elm is a kind of wood
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query about a conductor named Wood, perhaps Sir Henry Wood of the Proms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like a person's name (Sir Henry Wood, founder-conductor of the Proms) but it is just a tree; 'about' puts the wood and 'as' inside the series.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel master leads the music in a chapel or cathedral choir, hence a director of music.

clue.text: Flipping teacher drinking at college dance

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole assembled build backwards
the teacher drinks the next pieces, so they go inside

parts.note: a guru is a spiritual teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about a teacher boozing at college and then dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts AT and C inside the teacher, giving GURATCU, and 'Flipping' turns the whole thing backwards; the surface reads 'Flipping' as a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for taking to the floor energetically is a slangy way of saying to dance.

clue.text: Really shows skill penning two articles

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the articles are written inside

parts.note: art is skill, so what shows skill can be read as art
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A remark that someone genuinely shows talent writing a pair of newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles here are grammatical ones, not newspaper pieces; 'penning' puts both inside the skill word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning fundamentally or truly, so a fair swap for really.

clue.text: Vehicle's position in climbing event

indicators.note: position goes in the climbing event, so it is placed inside
in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a race is a sporting event
state means condition or position

explanation.surface: A remark about where a car stands in a hill-climb race.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' joining definition to wordplay. RACE climbing gives ECAR, with STATE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a long body and a rear door for luggage is a type of vehicle; the 's reads as is.

clue.text: Lanza beginning to mime opera piece? Not so

indicators.note: the beginning of the word mime is its first letter
not removes the word so that follows it

parts.note: an arioso is a melodious recitative in opera
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenor called Lanza starting to mime an operatic number, then denying it.
explanation.walkthrough: An arioso is an operatic passage between aria and recitative; 'Not so' removes its last two letters, and 'beginning to' takes M from 'mime'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario Lanza was the American tenor and film star, so his first name answers the surname.

clue.text: Reserve team in decline

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or reserve player
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A football report on a reserve team going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink or die down is to decline, both verbs of lessening.

clue.text: Enclosure with first of letters, look, in ordinary language

parts.note: enc. is the standard abbreviation for an enclosure in a letter

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word letters

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A note on a letter's enclosure, written plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase describes a message sent uncoded, in plain words rather than cipher.

clue.text: TV game show song?

definitions.meaning: the quiz show where contestants climb towards a top cash prize
the Cole Porter song from High Society, sung by Bing Crosby and Grace Kelly

explanation.definitionFit: The title names both the long-running quiz programme and the Cole Porter duet it borrowed its name from.

clue.text: Small axe that desperate revolutionary carried

indicators.note: the jumbled word carries the revolutionary, holding him inside
desperate suggests something in a wild state, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary

explanation.surface: A desperate rebel brandishing a hand axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' rearranges the word that as HATT, and 'carried' puts the revolutionary inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a short-handled axe used with one hand.

clue.text: Book about English Cricket Club saved by scholar

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: saved by means held within, so the scholar encloses the next pieces

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A book about a cricket club rescued from ruin by an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's novel bears this title, so it is a book.

clue.text: See 7
Justify angry tirade after conflict

indicators.note: after places the tirade behind the conflict

parts.note: war is conflict
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A demand to defend a furious outburst made after a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To give grounds for something is to justify it, a verb sense of warrant.

clue.text: Ring French friend about fake oriental art

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the fake

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
ami is French for friend
to rig is to fix or fake a result

explanation.surface: Phoning a French pal about some counterfeit Asian art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes is an art from the East.

clue.text: Near end of flight in the dark

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of flight

explanation.surface: A plane nearly at the end of its flight in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn; the dark is a common noun synonym.

clue.text: Had claret diluted for church

indicators.note: diluted wine is altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone watered down their red wine, perhaps communion wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a large church containing a bishop's throne.

clue.text: Programme I came across in desk

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the desk

parts.note: a table can serve as a desk
taken as written
met means came across

explanation.surface: Someone found a schedule lying on their desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of events or times is a programme.

clue.text: Got hold of peculiar percussion instrument

parts.note: snared means caught or got hold of
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone acquired an odd drum or other percussion piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a drum with wires underneath, a type of percussion instrument.

clue.text: Road ran out leading to principality

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A road that ran out leading to a small mountain country.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small principality in the Pyrenees.

clue.text: Precious stone from me borne by courier heading off

indicators.note: borne by means carried within, so the courier holds the word me
heading off removes the first letter of the courier

parts.note: a herald is a messenger or courier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gem delivered from me by a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves ERALD, and 'borne by' puts me inside it; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The emerald is a green gemstone, a precious stone.

clue.text: Catch girl with nothing on

indicators.note: on places nothing after the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to catch a girl wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to catch an animal with a noosed rope.

clue.text: Fast runner, potentially, always allowed to go round

indicators.note: to go round means allowed surrounds the word always

parts.note: let means allowed
ever means always

explanation.surface: A promising sprinter always permitted to run laps.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, which will become a fast runner in time.

clue.text: Nonsense verse about one on top of Christmas tree

indicators.note: the jumbled verse goes about the next pieces
nonsense rearranges the word verse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of Christmas

explanation.surface: Silly poetry about the star on top of the Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonsense' turns VERSE into SERVE, around I and C. The service tree is a European tree related to the rowan.
explanation.definitionFit: The service tree is a kind of tree, related to the rowan and whitebeam.

clue.text: One of a broken set daughter brought in anxious to mend

indicators.note: the daughter is brought into the next letters
anxious suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred around

explanation.surface: A daughter brought in, eager to repair an incomplete set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anxious' scrambles TO MEND to ODMENT, and D goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover piece, something left from an incomplete set.

clue.text: Number pass inside producing voucher

indicators.note: the pass goes inside the number

parts.note: ten is a number
OK means pass or approve

explanation.surface: A ticket number checked inside to produce a voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a voucher exchangeable for goods.

clue.text: Pub with a restaurant

parts.note: a tavern is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub with a dining room attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant.

clue.text: Designate member to go aboard European vessel

indicators.note: going aboard puts the member inside the vessel

parts.note: an ark is a vessel, like Noah's
an arm is a limb, a member

explanation.surface: Appointing a crew member to join a European ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark is to set aside or designate for a purpose.

clue.text: Scottish playwright taken to right gate

indicators.note: taken to means the right is attached after the playwright

parts.note: J M Barrie wrote Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A Scottish dramatist escorted to the correct gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is a gate or bar blocking passage.

clue.text: Nursery, good meeting place around wooded area of Warwickshire

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire, an English county
a centre is a place where people gather

explanation.surface: A nursery is a good place to meet near Warwickshire woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden is the ancient forest of Warwickshire, a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden centre is a shop selling plants, a nursery in the horticultural sense.
